story_context.protagonist: Dr. José Manuel Rodríguez Delgado (Yale Neurophysiologist)
story_context.inciting_incident: Unarmed inside a bullring, Delgado pressed a radio transmitter button as a 1,100-pound fighting bull charged at full speed—freezing the beast inches away.
story_context.scientific_truth: A radio-triggered electrode implanted in the caudate nucleus jammed the motor-aggression gearbox with a 1-milliamp electrical override.

physical_metaphor: Caudate nucleus electrode acting as an emergency hydraulic kill-switch overriding motor drive gears.
paradox_statement: A charging thousand-pound bull skidded to a dead halt because a scientist pressed a radio button.
dissonance_trigger: Millions of years of violent survival instinct were overridden in 0.2 seconds by a radio wave.
core_facts: In 1965, Yale neuroscientist José Delgado demonstrated wireless intracortical stimulation using his 'stimoceiver' implant in the caudate nucleus, arresting motor aggression in real time.

story_context.inciting_incident: Volunteers wept as they described every sensory detail of being lost in a shopping mall at age five—until researchers revealed the event never happened.
story_context.scientific_truth: Every time a memory is recalled, hippocampal circuits unlock into a malleable liquid state, splicing external suggestions directly into original neural wiring.

physical_metaphor: Hippocampal memory recall as opening a wet wax master-tape where new audio tracks overwrite original grooves before re-hardening.
paradox_statement: Your most vivid childhood memory can be completely fabricated in three short conversations.
dissonance_trigger: Human memory is not a read-only vault; every act of remembering rewrites the original file.
core_facts: Loftus and Pickrell (1995) demonstrated that suggestive interviewing implants rich episodic false memories by exploiting hippocampal memory reconsolidation plasticity.
